stories.headline: Babiš cancels Budapest CPAC trip, returns mid-flight due to suspected arson at Czech defense facility
stories.summary: Prime Minister Andrej Babiš cancelled his trip to the CPAC Hungary conference and turned his plane around mid-flight after a fire broke out at a defense facility in Pardubice. Czech authorities are investigating the incident as suspected terrorism linked to an anti-Israel group claiming responsibility.

stories.headline: Tens of thousands rally in Prague against Babiš government in largest protest since 2019
stories.summary: Massive anti-government demonstrations took place in Prague's Letná park, with protesters expressing concerns about democratic backsliding under Prime Minister Babiš. The protests drew attendees from across the Czech Republic and marked the largest such demonstration since 2019.

stories.headline: President Pavel conducts regional visits while criticizing government defense spending
stories.summary: President Petr Pavel visited the Central Bohemia region, including stops in Nymburk and meetings with local officials and citizens. During his visits, Pavel continued to criticize the government's planned defense budget as insufficient for NATO commitments.

stories.headline: Dispute emerges over Czech NATO summit representation amid defense spending criticism
stories.summary: A political dispute developed between President Pavel and PM Babiš over who should represent Czech Republic at the July NATO summit in Turkey. This comes amid ongoing criticism from NATO allies about Czech defense spending falling short of commitments.

stories.headline: Czech Republic signs cooperation agreement with Texas
stories.summary: Deputy PM Karel Havlíček signed a historic cooperation deal with Texas and opened a Czech House in Austin, highlighting business ties and the Czech-American community in Texas. The visit also included discussions with Lockheed Martin about F-35 deliveries.
